items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to excess disability insurance
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5760

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to excess disability
insurance

 
PURPOSE:

This bill creates a new kind of business disability-related coverage to
protect businesses, and individuals associated with such businesses,
from catastrophic loss where the limits of a primary disability insur-
ance policy in force may be inadequate to properly cover losses relative
to a business' financial circumstances, or where no primary business-re-
lated disability insurance coverage can be obtained in the authorized
insurer market by such business.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill establishes a new type of insurance, "catastrophic
business disruption insurance," intended to protect businesses from
financial loss caused by an individual integral to the successful func-
tioning of the business becoming disabled due to sickness, ailment or
bodily injury. Catastrophic business interruption insurance would pay
claims monies to a business when the limits of a primary business disa-
bility-related policy has been reached, or where such a primary policy
cannot be obtained in the authorized insurer market. Catastrophic busi-
ness disruption insurance would cover the overhead expenses of the busi-
ness or the costs of a buy/sell agreement.

Section 2 of the bill re-numbers former paragraph 32 of Section 1113(a)
of the Insurance Law as paragraph 33.

Section 3 of the bill adds new paragraph 32 to Section 2105 of the
Insurance Law to authorize excess line brokers to sell catastrophic
business disruption insurance in the excess line market.

Section 4 of the bill amends Section 4101 of the Insurance Law to add
catastrophic business disruption insurance to the list of "non-basic
kinds of insurance."

Section 5 of the bill amends Section 4103 of the Insurance Law to estab-
lish stock insurer paid-in capital and paid-in surplus requirements of
$100,000 and $50,000, respectively, for catastrophic business disruption
insurance.

Section 6 of the bill amends Section 4107 of the Insurance Law to estab-
lish domestic mutual insurer initial surplus and maintain surplus
requirements of $100,000 for each category in connection with
catastrophic business disruption insurance.

Section 8 of the bill establishes an immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Catastrophic business disruption insurance is a coverage that provides a
layer of insurance over the maximum benefit obtainable through author-
ized insurers, or in instances when no such coverage can be obtained at
all. Most authorized disability insurers do not write business forms of
disability insurance, and the few that do offer limited benefits. Busi-
nesses, especially those that are functionally dependent on key employ-
ees or business owners, risk failure in the event that the individual
integral to their success becomes disabled due to sickness, ailment or
bodily injury. The trickle-down impact on other employees of the busi-
ness enterprise is real world, and can be financially devastating to
such employees and their families.

Catastrophic business disruption insurance can cushion the negative
consequences of a key person disability event by providing funds to
cover business overhead expenses such as employee salaries, rent, utili-
ties costs, bank loans, equipment purchase and maintenance, computer
systems maintenance and all other expense facets associated with running
a business, or can cover the cost of a buy/sell agreement.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

A.10698 of 2018 A.2896 of 2019-20

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No cost to the state; taxes associated with the sale of excess line
policies will generate revenue for the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
